title: Derive per-table OR filters when the OR sits under a root AND (JoinDependentFilterRule after distributivity)
hypothesis: In q19 (347ms, the 4th slowest template), the part scan has NO filters: 2M rows go into the build side. The lineitem scan has no l_quantity filter: 15M rows probe the join (0.62s CPU), then a 0.39s FILTER evaluates the big OR and leaves 1,170 rows. JoinDependentFilterRule (src/optimizer/rule/join_dependent_filter.cpp) exists to derive per-table filters from an OR of ANDs, but Apply() returns early unless the OR is the ROOT expression (is_root). DistributivityRule is registered first (optimizer.cpp:52, vs :69) and factors the common terms (p_partkey=l_partkey, l_shipmode, l_shipinstruct) out of q19's OR, so the root becomes AND(common..., OR(rest)). The rule never fires. The same happens whenever a WHERE has an OR of cross-table ANDs plus other conjuncts, for example the q07 shape (n1='FRANCE' AND n2='GERMANY') OR (n1='GERMANY' AND n2='FRANCE') alongside join predicates. EVIDENCE: I appended the derived filters by hand: AND ((p_brand=.. AND p_container IN .. AND p_size BETWEEN ..) OR ...x3) AND ((l_quantity>=9 AND l_quantity<=19) OR ...x3). q19 went from 358ms to 173/181ms hot with the same result (41150783.5184). The part build shrinks to a few thousand rows, which also lets a join BF reach the lineitem scan.
plan:
In src/optimizer/rule/join_dependent_filter.cpp only:
(1) Move the derivation (ExtractConjunctedExpressions per child, then intersect the table indices across all children, building OR-of-per-table-ANDs) out of Apply into a file-local static `unique_ptr<Expression> DeriveFilter(BoundConjunctionExpression &or_expr)`. It returns nullptr when it is not eligible or derives nothing. Keep the existing eligibility check: at least one child is an AND that references several tables.
(2) In Apply, keep the op-type and is_root checks. If the root is CONJUNCTION_OR, behave exactly as today. If the root is CONJUNCTION_AND, loop over its direct children. For each child that is CONJUNCTION_OR, call DeriveFilter. Flatten the result into individual derived conjuncts, and keep each one only if no existing child of the root AND is Equals() to it. This dedupe is REQUIRED: the rewriter re-applies rules until fixpoint, and without it the rule loops forever. If anything was added, return a copy of the root AND with the new children appended and set changes_made. Otherwise return nullptr.
(3) The root matcher (a ConjunctionExpressionMatcher with SOME child conjunction) already matches an AND with an OR child, so no matcher change should be needed. Verify this.
CHECK BEFORE THE BENCH: EXPLAIN q19.m0 must show the p_brand/p_container/p_size OR filter on the part scan and an l_quantity filter on the lineitem scan. Run q19 and q07 and compare results with the current build. Confirm the planner finishes (no rewriter loop) on q19, q07 and a query with nested ORs. No header changes and no setting changes.
expected_gain: q19 about -45 to -50% (measured 358 -> ~177ms with manually derived filters), which is about -4% on the geomean by itself. q07 may gain if its nation OR is in the same AND-rooted shape. Other templates are unaffected.
generality: Any query whose WHERE/join filter has an OR of ANDs across tables alongside other conjuncts, or where distributivity factored out common terms. This is common in BI-generated filters and multi-segment predicates. The derived filters are implied by the original predicate, so results cannot change. Possible slowdown: the derived filters are evaluated in addition to the original OR. When they are unselective, that adds a small scan-filter cost, about what the existing root-OR path already accepts.
risk: Low-medium. The diff is contained to one file. The main risk is non-termination in the rewriter fixpoint loop if the dedupe is wrong, so test planning on several OR queries. Smaller risks: duplicated expressions, and cardinality estimates that change join order elsewhere. Wrong results are impossible as long as the derived terms are only ANDed onto the original.
